title.narrative: Crossborder emergency response in WASH and Protection to the crisis in Uvira

description.narrative: An integrated WASH and Protection intervention for more than 48,000 people across Uvira territory in DRC and Bujumbura province in Burundi, with flexibility to adapt activities as transit sites shift. The program links safe water, sanitation, and hygiene promotion with GBV case management, psychosocial support, and child protection, ensuring 92% of beneficiaries receive services in both sectors. WASH activities include rehabilitating health facilities, installing latrines and water points, and conducting hygiene campaigns, while Protection interventions provide dignity kits, counseling, community centers, and referral pathways aligned with international standards.

recipient-country.narrative: IRC will provide technical supervision of WASH interventions in Burundi to ensure coherence and alignment with SPHERE standards. IRC will conduct protection monitoring and security audits, and establish a community protection center (CPC) to welcome women and girls, including survivors, children, persons with disabilities, and child-friendly spaces (counseling office, recreational activities).The project will provide psychosocial support and case management sessions as well as recreational activities, and will identify and strengthen the capacities of community leaders and activists in legal assistance in matters related to protection.

IRC will provide training for service providers, community health workers, and local hygiene committees on IPC, and will likewise build capacity in IPC awareness-raising techniques within these community structures, in collaboration with the Ministry of Health. Technical supervision of WASH interventions will be provided to ensure coherence and alignment with SPHERE and cluster standards. Technical supervision of Protection interventions through IRC's technical experts in DRC will also be provided.
